chapter_title: Narration, Modifiers, Connectors, Synonyms and Antonyms

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: 'He said to me, "I am writing an academic paper today."'

options.label: A
options.text: He told me that he was writing an academic paper that day.

options.label: B
options.text: He said to me that I am writing an academic paper today.

options.label: C
options.text: He told me that he is writing an academic paper today.

options.label: D
options.text: He said that he had been writing an academic paper that day.

questions.correct_answer_text: He told me that he was writing an academic paper that day.
questions.explanation: When reporting in past tense ('said to me' -> 'told me'), present continuous 'am writing' shifts to past continuous 'was writing', and 'today' changes to 'that day'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The teacher said, "The Earth revolves around the sun."'

options.label: A
options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the sun.

options.label: B
options.text: The teacher said that the Earth revolved around the sun.

options.label: C
options.text: The teacher told that the Earth had revolved around the sun.

options.label: D
options.text: The teacher said whether the Earth revolves around the sun.

questions.correct_answer_text: The teacher said that the Earth revolves around the sun.
questions.explanation: Universal scientific truths and geographical facts do not undergo tense backshift in indirect speech; the present simple remains unchanged.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'Rahim said, "I bought these books yesterday."'

options.label: A
options.text: Rahim said that he had bought those books the previous day.

options.label: B
options.text: Rahim said that he bought these books yesterday.

options.label: C
options.text: Rahim told that he has bought those books the previous day.

options.label: D
options.text: Rahim said that he had bought these books yesterday.

questions.correct_answer_text: Rahim said that he had bought those books the previous day.
questions.explanation: Simple past 'bought' backshifts to past perfect 'had bought', 'these' becomes 'those', and 'yesterday' becomes 'the previous day'.

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: 'She said, "I have finished my homework."'

options.label: A
options.text: She said that she had finished her homework.

options.label: B
options.text: She said that she has finished her homework.

options.label: C
options.text: She said that she finished her homework.

options.label: D
options.text: She told that I had finished my homework.

questions.correct_answer_text: She said that she had finished her homework.
questions.explanation: Present perfect 'have finished' backshifts to past perfect 'had finished', and pronoun 'my' changes to 'her'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The doctor said to the patient, "You must take this medicine twice daily."'

options.label: A
options.text: The doctor advised the patient that he had to take that medicine twice daily.

options.label: B
options.text: The doctor told the patient that he must to take this medicine.

options.label: C
options.text: The doctor asked the patient if he took that medicine.

options.label: D
options.text: The doctor said the patient should take medicine.

questions.correct_answer_text: The doctor advised the patient that he had to take that medicine twice daily.
questions.explanation: In indirect speech, ordinary modal obligation 'must' often converts into 'had to', and 'this' converts into 'that'.

topics.topic_name: Narration of Interrogative and Imperative Sentences

questions.question: Change into indirect speech: 'He said to me, "Are you going to the library today?"'

options.label: A
options.text: He asked me if I was going to the library that day.

options.label: B
options.text: He asked me that if I am going to the library today.

options.label: C
options.text: He told me was I going to the library that day.

options.label: D
options.text: He enquired me whether you were going to the library.

questions.correct_answer_text: He asked me if I was going to the library that day.
questions.explanation: For yes/no questions, the reporting verb becomes 'asked', the connector is 'if / whether', and the word order becomes assertive ('I was going').

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The stranger said to me, "Where do you live?"'

options.label: A
options.text: The stranger asked me where I lived.

options.label: B
options.text: The stranger asked me that where did I live.

options.label: C
options.text: The stranger enquired where do I live.

options.label: D
options.text: The stranger asked me where I had lived.

questions.correct_answer_text: The stranger asked me where I lived.
questions.explanation: In WH-questions, the WH-word ('where') serves as the connector, and 'do you live' becomes assertive past 'I lived'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The officer said to the soldiers, "Halt and keep quiet!"'

options.label: A
options.text: The officer commanded the soldiers to halt and keep quiet.

options.label: B
options.text: The officer asked the soldiers that they should halt and keep quiet.

options.label: C
options.text: The officer said to the soldiers to halt and keep quiet.

options.label: D
options.text: The officer wished that the soldiers halted.

questions.correct_answer_text: The officer commanded the soldiers to halt and keep quiet.
questions.explanation: In imperative sentences expressing military orders, the reporting verb is 'commanded / ordered' followed by the infinitive 'to + verb'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The doctor said to the patient, "Do not smoke cigarettes anymore."'

options.label: A
options.text: The doctor advised the patient not to smoke cigarettes anymore.

options.label: B
options.text: The doctor forbade the patient not to smoke cigarettes anymore.

options.label: C
options.text: The doctor asked the patient that do not smoke.

options.label: D
options.text: The doctor told to the patient to not smoke.

questions.correct_answer_text: The doctor advised the patient not to smoke cigarettes anymore.
questions.explanation: Negative imperatives convert into 'advised / told + object + not to + verb'. Note: 'forbade' already contains a negative, so 'forbade... not to' is redundant.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'Father said to me, "May you pass the examination with distinction!"' (Optative)

options.label: A
options.text: Father wished that I might pass the examination with distinction.

options.label: B
options.text: Father prayed that you may pass the examination with distinction.

options.label: C
options.text: Father told me to pass the examination with distinction.

options.label: D
options.text: Father said that I will pass the examination with distinction.

questions.correct_answer_text: Father wished that I might pass the examination with distinction.
questions.explanation: Optative sentences of blessing/wish use reporting verbs 'wished / prayed that' with subject + 'might' + base verb.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The boy said, "Hurrah! Our school team has won the championship!"'

options.label: A
options.text: The boy exclaimed with joy that their school team had won the championship.

options.label: B
options.text: The boy cried out that our school team has won the championship.

options.label: C
options.text: The boy told happily that their school team won.

options.label: D
options.text: The boy shouted that his school team had won.

questions.correct_answer_text: The boy exclaimed with joy that their school team had won the championship.
questions.explanation: Joyful interjections ('Hurrah!') convert to 'exclaimed with joy that', and present perfect 'has won' shifts to 'had won'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The pedestrian said, "Alas! The poor beggar is dead!"'

options.label: A
options.text: The pedestrian exclaimed with sorrow that the poor beggar was dead.

options.label: B
options.text: The pedestrian cried alas that the beggar died.

options.label: C
options.text: The pedestrian lamented that the poor beggar is dead.

options.label: D
options.text: The pedestrian said with sadness that the beggar has died.

questions.correct_answer_text: The pedestrian exclaimed with sorrow that the poor beggar was dead.
questions.explanation: Sorrowful interjections ('Alas!') convert to 'exclaimed with sorrow / grief that' followed by past tense 'was dead'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'She said, "What a breathtaking sunset it is!"'

options.label: A
options.text: She exclaimed with wonder that it was a very breathtaking sunset.

options.label: B
options.text: She said that what a breathtaking sunset it was.

options.label: C
options.text: She asked whether it was a breathtaking sunset.

options.label: D
options.text: She exclaimed that it is a very breathtaking sunset.

questions.correct_answer_text: She exclaimed with wonder that it was a very breathtaking sunset.
questions.explanation: Exclamations of wonder transform into 'exclaimed with wonder/admiration that + subject + was a very + adjective'.

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'He said, "Good morning, my dear friends!"'

options.label: A
options.text: He wished his dear friends good morning.

options.label: B
options.text: He said good morning to his friends.

options.label: C
options.text: He bade good morning to his friends.

options.label: D
options.text: He greeted that good morning friends.

questions.correct_answer_text: He wished his dear friends good morning.
questions.explanation: Salutations like 'Good morning' or 'Happy New Year' use the reporting verb 'wished' ('wished his friends good morning').

questions.question: Change into indirect: 'The traveler said, "Farewell, my beloved homeland!"'

options.label: A
options.text: The traveler bade farewell to his beloved homeland.

options.label: B
options.text: The traveler wished farewell to his homeland.

options.label: C
options.text: The traveler said farewell to his homeland.

options.label: D
options.text: The traveler exclaimed farewell his homeland.

questions.correct_answer_text: The traveler bade farewell to his beloved homeland.
questions.explanation: Parting words like 'Farewell' or 'Good night' use the reporting verb 'bade' (past of bid: 'bade farewell to...').

questions.question: Identify the noun adjective used as a pre-modifier in: 'She booked a luxury train ticket to Sylhet.'

options.label: A
options.text: train (Noun functioning as an adjective modifying 'ticket')

questions.correct_answer_text: train (Noun functioning as an adjective modifying 'ticket')
questions.explanation: A noun used to modify another subsequent noun is called a noun adjective (or noun pre-modifier); here 'train' modifies 'ticket'.

questions.question: In the phrase 'the crying baby', what grammatical element functions as the pre-modifier?
questions.explanation: 'Crying' is a present participle (verb+ing) pre-modifying the noun 'baby' by describing an active state.

questions.question: In 'He visited his ancestral home', which word serves as a possessive pre-modifier?
questions.explanation: 'His' is a possessive determiner/pronoun functioning as a pre-modifier of the noun phrase.

questions.question: Use an intensifier to pre-modify the adjective: 'The examination question paper was ______ challenging.'
questions.explanation: Intensifiers are adverbs of degree (extremely, very, remarkably) that pre-modify adjectives or other adverbs.

questions.question: In the phrase 'a retired army officer', what is 'retired'?

options.label: A
options.text: Past participle functioning as an adjective pre-modifier

questions.correct_answer_text: Past participle functioning as an adjective pre-modifier
questions.explanation: 'Retired' is a past participle used adjectivally to pre-modify the noun 'officer'.

questions.question: Identify the appositive post-modifier in: 'Kazi Nazrul Islam, our national poet, composed inspirational songs.'
questions.explanation: An appositive is a noun phrase placed adjacent to another noun to rename or further identify it ('our national poet').

questions.question: In 'The book on the corner table belongs to the library', what is 'on the corner table'?
questions.explanation: The prepositional phrase follows the head noun 'The book' and acts as an adjectival post-modifier specifying which book.

questions.question: Identify the infinitive phrase post-modifying the noun in: 'He has an unyielding determination to win the tournament.'
questions.explanation: The infinitive phrase 'to win the tournament' post-modifies the abstract noun 'determination'.

questions.question: In 'The girl singing a patriotic song on stage is my cousin', what is 'singing a patriotic song on stage'?
questions.explanation: The participial phrase 'singing...' post-modifies the subject noun 'The girl', functioning adjectivally.

questions.question: What is a 'Dangling Modifier'?

options.label: A
options.text: A modifying phrase that lacks a clear or logical subject to modify in the main clause

options.label: B
options.text: A punctuation mark omitted at the end of a sentence

options.label: C
options.text: An adjective that has no comparative form

questions.correct_answer_text: A modifying phrase that lacks a clear or logical subject to modify in the main clause
questions.explanation: A dangling modifier occurs when an introductory participial phrase does not logically connect with the grammatical subject following it (e.g. 'Walking in the park, a snake bit him').

questions.question: Which sentence connector expresses CONTRAST between two statements?
questions.explanation: 'However' is an adversative transitional connector showing contradiction or contrast between statements.

questions.question: Choose the appropriate connector showing CAUSE AND EFFECT: 'He violated company regulations repeatedly. ______, he was dismissed from his post.'
questions.explanation: 'Consequently' (or 'Therefore' / 'As a result') introduces a direct outcome or logical consequence of preceding facts.

questions.question: Which sentence connector is used to introduce an ADDITIONAL supporting point?
questions.explanation: 'Moreover' (along with 'Furthermore' and 'In addition') reinforces an argument with extra supporting evidence.

questions.question: Fill in the blank with the best discourse marker: 'Trees give us shade and fruit. ______, they absorb harmful greenhouse carbon dioxide.'
questions.explanation: 'Besides' functions as a cohesive device adding further value or benefit to the preceding statement.

questions.question: Which connector correctly introduces an EXEMPLIFICATION or clarification?
questions.explanation: 'For instance' (or 'For example') is the standard discourse marker providing an illustrative specific example.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'diligent' in academic contexts?
questions.explanation: 'Diligent' means having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work; industrious is a direct synonym.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'benevolent'?
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' denotes goodwill, generosity, and charitable kindness.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'eradicate' in 'efforts to eradicate illiteracy'?
questions.explanation: 'Eradicate' means to tear out by the roots; to completely destroy or remove.

questions.question: What is the synonym of the word 'lucid' in 'a lucid explanation of the grammatical rule'?
questions.explanation: 'Lucid' means expressed clearly and easily understood.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'pinnacle' in 'the pinnacle of his scientific career'?
questions.explanation: 'Pinnacle' refers to the most successful point or culmination; 'zenith' is its exact synonym.

questions.question: What is the antonym of the adjective 'transient' in 'transient earthly pleasures'?
questions.explanation: 'Transient' means passing quickly or temporary. Its direct opposite is 'permanent' or 'enduring'.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'obscure' in 'an obscure ancient manuscript'?
questions.explanation: 'Obscure' means little known or difficult to understand; 'famous' or 'clear' is its antonym.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'hostile' in 'a hostile diplomatic reception'?
questions.explanation: 'Hostile' means unfriendly, aggressive, or antagonistic. Its direct antonym is 'friendly' or 'cordial'.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'frugal' in 'his frugal household spending'?
questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means careful and sparing with money; its antonym is 'extravagant' or 'profligate'.

questions.question: What is the antonym of 'culpable' in 'culpable negligence'?
questions.explanation: 'Culpable' means deserving blame or censure; its antonym is 'blameless' or 'innocent'.

questions.question: Which punctuation mark is used to connect two closely related independent clauses without a coordinating conjunction?
questions.explanation: A semicolon joins two independent clauses that are closely linked in thought when no coordinating conjunction (and, but) is used.

questions.question: What is the error in: 'Its a beautiful sunny morning in Dhaka.'?

options.label: A
options.text: Misuse of possessive 'Its' instead of contraction 'It's' (It is)

questions.correct_answer_text: Misuse of possessive 'Its' instead of contraction 'It's' (It is)
questions.explanation: 'It's' is the contracted form of 'It is', whereas 'Its' without an apostrophe is a possessive pronoun (e.g. 'The dog wagged its tail').

questions.question: Which sentence is correctly punctuated?

options.label: A
options.text: "Where are you traveling, sir?" the conductor asked.

options.label: B
options.text: "Where are you traveling, sir?", the conductor asked.

options.label: C
options.text: "Where are you traveling sir?" The conductor asked.

options.label: D
options.text: Where are you traveling, sir? The conductor asked.

questions.correct_answer_text: "Where are you traveling, sir?" the conductor asked.
questions.explanation: Direct speech in quotation marks with question mark does not take an additional comma, and the reporting tag continues in lowercase ('the conductor').

questions.question: When should the colon (:) be used according to standard punctuation rules?

options.label: A
options.text: To introduce a list, explanation, or direct quotation following a complete independent clause

options.label: C
options.text: Between a verb and its direct object

options.label: D
options.text: To separate syllables in a dictionary

questions.correct_answer_text: To introduce a list, explanation, or direct quotation following a complete independent clause
questions.explanation: A colon introduces an item, list, or explanation that clarifies a preceding complete sentence.

questions.question: Choose the correctly capitalized and punctuated sentence:

options.label: A
options.text: On Friday, Professor Rahman lectured on Shakespeare's tragedy, 'Hamlet'.

options.label: B
options.text: On friday, professor Rahman lectured on shakespeares tragedy, 'hamlet'.

options.label: C
options.text: On Friday, Professor rahman lectured on Shakespeare's Tragedy, 'Hamlet'.

options.label: D
options.text: On friday, Professor Rahman lectured on Shakespeare tragedy, Hamlet.

questions.correct_answer_text: On Friday, Professor Rahman lectured on Shakespeare's tragedy, 'Hamlet'.
questions.explanation: Proper days (Friday), formal academic titles with names (Professor Rahman), author names (Shakespeare's), and literary titles ('Hamlet') must be capitalized.

topics.topic_name: Passage Integration and Applied Grammar Synthesis

questions.question: In narrative conversion, what does 'tomorrow' transform into in indirect speech?

options.label: A
options.text: The next day (or the following day)

questions.correct_answer_text: The next day (or the following day)
questions.explanation: 'Tomorrow' shifts to 'the next day' or 'the following day' in indirect speech.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence connector: 'He worked round the clock. ______, he completed the software project before the deadline.'
questions.explanation: 'As a result' expresses the logical positive outcome of his continuous hard work.

questions.question: In 'The teacher explained the concept clearly', what is 'clearly'?

options.label: A
options.text: Adverb of manner post-modifying the verb 'explained'

questions.correct_answer_text: Adverb of manner post-modifying the verb 'explained'
questions.explanation: 'Clearly' is an adverb of manner post-modifying the transitive verb 'explained'.

questions.question: What is the synonym of 'indispensable' in 'English is indispensable for international communication'?
questions.explanation: 'Indispensable' means absolutely necessary, essential, or vital.

questions.question: Identify the punctuation mark needed before the list: 'The applicant brought the following documents ______ his passport, academic transcripts, and national ID.'
questions.explanation: A colon (:) is used after a complete independent introductory clause ('The applicant brought the following documents:') to introduce a list of items.
